battle.name: 厄瓜多爾獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 安第斯山麓至瓜亞基爾河口
battle.brief: 一八二〇年八月十日，基多市民與部分駐軍在聖弗朗西斯科廣場舉事，安第斯各城鎮隨後響應；一八二一年九月瓜亞基爾守軍反正，翌年五月二十四日至二十五日，蘇克雷率約兩千人於皮欎查山麓擊破皇家派軍，基多遂宣告成立厄瓜多爾共和國。燧發槍是兩方步兵骨幹，愛國派多購英國貨，射速與精度全靠它撐住。

kit.name: 燧發槍
kit.history: 击锤打火比火绳稳。线性列阵的射速和精度都靠它撑着。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方，一方是仍效忠西班牙王室的南美殖民當局：十八世紀末以來由秘魯總督轄區與基多「聖地亞哥王庭」管轄的克里奧爾殖民政府，正式部隊是西班牙王室的正規軍團與炮兵，民事一端是各城市議會與地方長官；另一方是基多與瓜亞基爾先後成立的愛國派自治政府及其民兵軍。1820年8月10日基多舉事之後，基多成立執委會，填補了1814年拉美各王廷解體所留下的權力真空，秘魯總督若阿金·德·拉·佩蘇埃拉拒絕承認基多執委會，改以軍力壓迫，對抗由政治轉為軍事。1821年9月24日瓜亞基爾駐軍與市民起義，瓜亞基爾另立自治政府，國王派官吏與守軍退往秘魯本土，海岸線與安第斯山區自此分成兩個陣營。1822年5月24日基多宣告成立厄瓜多爾共和國，同年9月21日波哥大條約把基多、瓜亞基爾與委內瑞拉、新格拉納達合組成大哥倫比亞聯邦，玻利瓦爾出任聯邦總統，蘇克雷任元帥，愛國派軍隊自此併入聯邦編制。雙方的兵員結構也根本不同：皇家派以受過線式操演的受薪正規兵為骨幹，輔以數量有限的殖民民兵；愛國派則以各教區臨時抽丁的民兵為主，軍官多為克里奧爾知識人與退役軍人，裝備與訓練參差，靠數量、地理與英國援助取勝。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were, on one side, the colonial authorities of Spanish South America still loyal to the Spanish crown: a criollo colonial government administered from the Audiencia of Quito under the Viceroyalty of Peru, its formal troops the crown's regular regiments and artillery and its civilian arm the municipal councils and local magistrates; on the other, the patriot autonomist governments of Quito and Guayaquil together with their militias. After the rising of 10 August 1820 in Quito, a junta took over and filled the power vacuum left by the abolition of the Spanish audiencias in 1814; the Viceroy of Peru Joaquín de la Pezuela refused to recognise the Quito junta's authority and turned instead to arms, so the confrontation moved from politics into open war. On 24 September 1821 the garrison and citizens of Guayaquil rose, Guayaquil set up its own autonomous government, and the royalist officials and troops fell back into Peru proper, leaving the coast and the Andean interior as two separate camps. On 24 May 1822 Quito proclaimed the Republic of Ecuador, and on 21 September 1822 the Treaty of Bogotá joined Quito, Guayaquil, Venezuela and New Granada into the federation of Gran Colombia, with Simón Bolívar as president and Sucre as marshal, the patriot armies passing into the federal command. The two sides' manpower structures were as different as their aims: the royalists built their army on salaried regulars drilled in the linear school, with only a thin colonial militia behind them, while the patriots fought with parish levies raised on a population basis, officered mostly by criollo intellectuals and retired soldiers, badly equipped and badly drilled, and winning on numbers, on ground, and on British aid.
people: 關鍵人物橫跨兩個陣營。安德烈斯·德·聖克魯斯是基多愛國派的核心之一：這位出身克里奧爾軍人家庭的主官，1820年8月10日在基多街頭響應起義，隨後出任自治政府的統兵者，翌年調往玻利維亞作戰陣亡；伯納多·德·查奧與塞巴斯蒂安·德·貝納文特一同在起義當夜推舉代表、接管市政，主持基多執委會。何塞·德·安特帕拉是基多《基多尼人報》的報人兼愛國派宣傳家，1820年10月在報上刊出公開的行動號召，1821年瓜亞基爾舉事時又被推到前台，隨後兩度入獄，最終流亡，他把志士的私人聚會寫成報紙專欄，為起義製造了輿論。胡安·德·貝拉斯科是策劃者之一，1820年8月10日以後主持基多行政，1834至1839年任厄瓜多爾總統。西班牙方面的關鍵人物是梅希亞：這位參加過半島戰爭的老將奉命率援軍南下，指望重新控制基多，卻在皮欎查把整個皇家派陣地葬送。安東尼奧·何塞·德·蘇克雷則是他的對手，出身加拉加斯的西班牙裔家庭，早年在西班牙軍中服役，參與委內瑞拉獨立，後來接管基多與玻利維亞戰線，1822年5月24日以不到三千人擊敗梅希亞並解放基多，隨即被玻利瓦爾任命為大哥倫比亞的第二號人物。炮兵軍官米勒出身阿根廷，卻熟悉歐洲炮術與英式火器，指挥愛國派砲隊並在皮欎查首日代蘇克雷主持陣地；更早的推手是費爾南多·德·羅卡福特，他在基多任職期間於1811年推動廢除奴役並禁止奴隸貿易，讓黑奴與混血社群獲得支持獨立的理由。
peopleEn: The key figures span both camps. Andrés de Santa Cruz was one of the core of the Quito patriots: a commander from a criollo military family who answered the rising in the streets of Quito on 10 August 1820, became the military leader of the autonomous government, and was killed in action in Bolivia the following year; Bernardo de Zhao and Sebastián de Benavente chose the representatives and took over the municipal government on the night of the rising itself, and Zhao presided over the Quito junta. José de Antepara was the editor of Quito's El Quiteño and the propagandist of the patriot cause; in October 1820 he published an open call to action in the paper, was pushed to the front of the 1821 Guayaquil rising, was twice imprisoned and finally exiled, and by turning the patriots' private meetings into newspaper columns he built the public opinion that the rising needed. Juan de Velasco was one of the plotters and ran the Quito administration after 10 August 1820, and was president of Ecuador from 1834 to 1839. The decisive figure on the Spanish side was Melchor Aymerich, a veteran of the Peninsular War sent south with reinforcements to recover Quito, who buried the whole royalist position at Pichincha. His opposite number was Antonio José de Sucre, born of a Spanish family in Caracas, long in Spanish service, a veteran of the Venezuelan war of independence, who took over the Quito and Bolivian fronts and on 24 May 1822 defeated Aymerich with fewer than three thousand men and relieved Quito, after which Bolívar named him the second man of Gran Colombia. The artillery officer Guillermo Miller, an Argentine by birth but an expert in European gunnery and British ordnance, commanded the patriot batteries and on the first day at Pichincha directed the field while Sucre was hit. An earlier promoter was Fernando de Rocafuerte, who during his posting at Quito pushed in 1811 for the abolition of slavery and of the slave trade, giving enslaved and mixed-race people a concrete reason to support the patriot cause.
kits: 燧發槍是這場戰爭裡兩方步兵的骨幹。十八世紀中葉以後，英國與西班牙的步兵普遍以燧發機制取代火繩，殖民地軍隊使用的多是英國「褐貝絲」式的燧發步槍，口徑約零點五四與零點五八英吋，附插管刺刀；西班牙王室的常備團在拿破崙戰爭後已經換裝，但補充海外殖民地的裝備往往直接由英國或愛爾蘭工場訂製，1820年代仍在源源運抵。愛國派同樣靠英國商人取得火器：倫敦與利物浦的武器商把燧發步槍、火藥、鉛彈與刺刀賣給南美進出口商，再由商船運到瓜亞基爾與卡亞俄，玻利瓦爾的智利盟友與英國私掠船也協助轉運。民兵裝備卻極不統一，獵槍、火繩手槍、砍刀、矛、投石索與農具同時出現在同一次出擊裡，裝載量、射程與射速都無法與制式槍相比。砲兵方面，愛國派在皮欎查擁有約八門四磅至六磅野戰砲與數門榴彈砲，由米勒率領；皇家派的砲組更完整，配備十二磅攻城砲，並以居高臨下的射角對付山脊上的愛國派陣地。安第斯山區的冷兵器並未退場，騎槍、佩劍、馬刀與長矛仍在近戰中發揮作用；瓜亞斯河上的獨木舟是補給的骨幹，後方物資靠騾、驢與牛群沿山道運轉，軍隊同時面臨缺糧、缺柴與雨季泥濘三重困難。
kitsEn: The flintlock musket was the backbone of the infantry on both sides. From the middle of the eighteenth century British and Spanish infantry in general had replaced the matchlock with the flint mechanism, and the guns carried by colonial troops were mostly British Brown Bess pattern flintlock muskets of about .54 and .58 calibre, fitted with socket bayonets. The crown's standing regiments had been re-equipped after the Napoleonic wars, but the replacements sent out to the overseas colonies continued to be ordered directly from British and Irish makers, and they kept arriving through the 1820s. The patriots obtained their arms from British merchants in the same way: London and Liverpool gunsmiths sold flintlock muskets, powder, lead and bayonets to South American traders, who shipped them to Guayaquil and Callao, with the aid of Bolívar's Chilean allies and of British privateers for the transshipment. Militia equipment, however, was extremely uneven; hunting guns, matchlock pistols, machetes, pikes, slings and farm tools all appeared in the same sortie, and none of them could match a regulation musket in charge, range or rate of fire. On the artillery side the patriots had at Pichincha roughly eight field guns of four to six pounds and several howitzers under Miller, while the royalist battery was better organised, with twelve-pounder siege pieces, and used its plunging angle against the patriot positions on the ridge. Cold weapons had not disappeared in the Andes: lances, sabres, swords and long pikes still mattered in close fighting, and the canoes on the Guayas river were the artery of supply, with provisions carried inland by mules, donkeys and driven cattle along the mountain tracks, the army at the same time pressed by short rations, lack of fuel and the mud of the rainy season.
tactics: 1820年8月10日基多的起義是一場典型的城市奪權：志士在「水銀街」一帶的店鋪與宅邸間傳遞消息，於夜間同時出動，控制廣場、兵營與軍械庫，切斷總督府與王廷之間的傳令，再於清晨聚集在聖弗朗西斯科廣場公開宣告首聲獨立；此後各教區的民兵按同一節奏起事，縱火焚燒殖民官吏的宅邸與莊園，使對方無法集中兵力逐個應付。1821年9月24日的瓜亞基爾起義則由駐軍內應先行奪取兵營與砲台，城市民兵隨後接管碼頭與河口，切斷海上援軍的登陸點。內陸的消耗戰交給游擊隊：米科斯、喬科與曼薩比的營地民兵在山間小徑上襲擊皇家派的糧隊與郵差，切斷基多與海岸之間的連絡；愛國派主力則在蘇克雷率領下由安第斯向海岸反攻，1822年的海岸遠征把皇家派殘餘據點逐個拔除。皮欎查的戰法最能說明地形對火力的限制：愛國派搶先佔據山脊與制高點，以線式排槍向下射擊，砲兵在坡面後方展開，以俯射砲火壓制對方步兵；狹窄的山道無法展開縱隊，皇家派多出的人數只能擠在前沿，首日蘇克雷腿部與頭部受傷後，軍務由米勒等人接手掌管，次日凌晨的總攻配合砲火摧毀數個陣地，皇家派最精銳的「女王團」在側翼崩潰，梅希亞率殘部連夜退回基多。整場戰事都在五月的雨季裡，山雨、濃霧、寒冷與泥濘同時削弱進攻者的體力與防守者的射擊精度。
tacticsEn: The rising of 10 August 1820 in Quito was a textbook urban seizure of power: the conspirators passed word among the shops and houses of the Calle de la Mercury, moved out together at night, took the square, the barracks and the armoury, cut the line of despatch between the viceregal government and the Audiencia, and then assembled at dawn in the Plaza de San Francisco to proclaim the first cry of independence. The parish militias rose in the same rhythm afterwards, burning the houses and estates of the colonial officials so that the royalist administration could never concentrate its forces against one rising at a time. The Guayaquil rising of 24 September 1821 began with an insider in the garrison seizing the barracks and the gun positions, after which the city militia took the quays and the river mouth and closed the landing places for sea reinforcements. The war of attrition in the interior was left to the irregulars: the montoneros of the Micos, the Choco and the Manabi country took to the mountain paths to raid royalist supply columns and couriers, cutting the line between Quito and the coast, while the patriot main body under Sucre drove from the Andes towards the coast, and the coastal campaign of 1822 rooted out one royalist foothold after another. The fighting at Pichincha shows the limit that terrain placed on firepower better than anything else. The patriots seized the ridge and the commanding heights first and fired linear volleys downhill, their guns deployed behind the slope to press the opposing infantry with plunging shot; the narrow tracks gave the royalist numbers no room to deploy, and their advantage in men could only be crowded onto the front. When Sucre was hit in the leg and the head on the first day, the command passed to Miller and the other officers, and the general assault at dawn on the second day broke several positions with the help of the guns, the royalist elite regiment known as the Regimiento de la Reina collapsing on the flank and Aymerich withdrawing with the remnants to Quito during the night. The whole engagement was fought in the rains of May, when mountain rain, mist, cold and mud crippled the attackers' strength and the defenders' shooting accuracy alike.
data: 可核對的數字集中在幾個節點。中文維基把厄瓜多爾獨立戰爭列為1820至1822年；起點是1820年8月10日基多的首聲獨立，當夜參與者為數百名市民、商人與部分駐軍，規模不大，卻在數日內擴散至聖多明各、里奧班巴、庫恩卡等安第斯城市。1821年9月24日瓜亞基爾舉事成功，同年9月瓜亞基爾自治政府成立，國王派在海岸只剩下少數據點。皮欎查一戰的雙方兵力，愛國派方面常引兩千人上下，不同記載在一千八百至二千二百之間，配砲約八門；皇家派方面常引三千至四千人，其中「女王團」約八百人為其精銳，另有從秘魯南下的援軍與砲組。蘇克雷在5月24日的交火中腿部與頭部受傷，當日傷亡數百；皇家派在25日崩潰，死傷逾千、被俘數百，火砲與軍械大量落入愛國派手中，砲數的說法不一，有記九門，亦有記十七門。梅希亞退入基多後守不住，隨即放棄城市向秘魯方向撤退，而基多在5月24日已宣布厄瓜多爾共和國成立。地理上，皮欎查距基多約四十公里，戰場在海拔三千至三千五百公尺的山麓，最高峰逾四千七百公尺；自瓜亞基爾沿陸路到基多，傳統行軍需時六至十日，運輸主要靠騾、驢、馬與牛。城市規模方面，1820年代的基多人口約二萬至三萬，瓜亞基爾約二萬，全國人口不過數十萬，各教區按人口比例抽丁組成民兵連。往後的制度日期也清楚：1822年9月21日波哥大條約組成大哥倫比亞聯邦，1830年4月《瓜亞基爾議定書》宣告厄瓜多爾分離，1830年11月胡安·波索爾福出任首任總統，1832年《安孔條約》把加拉帕戈斯群島劃歸厄瓜多爾。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked cluster around a few landmarks. Chinese Wikipedia dates the Ecuadorian War of Independence to 1820 to 1822. The starting point is the first cry of independence in Quito on 10 August 1820, in which a few hundred citizens, merchants and part of the garrison took part; small as it was, it spread within days to the Andean cities of Santo Domingo, Riobamba and Cuenca. The rising at Guayaquil succeeded on 24 September 1821, and in the same month the autonomous government of Guayaquil was set up, leaving the royalists with only a handful of strongholds on the coast. At Pichincha the usual figures are around two thousand men for the patriots, with accounts ranging from eighteen hundred to twenty-two hundred and about eight guns, against three to four thousand for the royalists, of whom the Regimiento de la Reina, roughly eight hundred strong, was the elite, together with reinforcements and artillery sent south from Peru. Sucre was hit in the leg and the head in the fighting of 24 May, with several hundred casualties on the patriot side that day; the royalist line collapsed on the 25th with more than a thousand killed or wounded and several hundred prisoners, and a large haul of guns and stores fell to the victors, the number of cannon being given variously as nine or as seventeen. Unable to hold Quito after his return, Aymerich abandoned the city and withdrew towards Peru, and on 24 May Quito had already proclaimed the Republic of Ecuador. Geographically, Pichincha lies about forty kilometres from Quito, the fighting was on slopes at three thousand to three thousand five hundred metres, and the summit of the volcano exceeds four thousand seven hundred metres; the traditional march from Guayaquil to Quito took six to ten days, and transport depended on mules, donkeys, horses and cattle. As for population, Quito held perhaps twenty to thirty thousand souls in the 1820s and Guayaquil about twenty thousand, in a country of no more than several hundred thousand, with each parish raising militia companies on a quota of men to its population. The subsequent constitutional dates are equally clear: the Treaty of Bogotá of 21 September 1822 created the federation of Gran Colombia, the Guayaquil Protocol of April 1830 declared the separation of Ecuador, Juan Posada became the first president in November 1830, and the Treaty of Ancón of 1832 assigned the Galapagos islands to Ecuador.
cause: 要理解這場戰爭為何會打成，須把三層原因疊在一起。最遠的一層是帝國本身的裂痕：1808年斐迪南七世退位引發的自由革命、拿破崙戰爭對西班牙海外能力的消耗、克里奧爾與半島人（peninsulares）在稅收、任官與貿易壟斷上的對立，以及聖地亞哥王庭對基多的長期壟斷，都讓「是否繼續效忠馬德里」成為可問的問題。1814年拉美各王庭被廢除後，基多自治政府一度成立又倒台；玻利維亞1809年的革命與1825年的獨立提供了榜樣；1811年羅卡福特在基多廢除奴役並禁止奴隸貿易，使黑奴與混血社群獲得明確的理由支持愛國派，到1820年，這些願望在基多已醞釀成一股可被點燃的政治力量。第二層是國際條件：玻利瓦爾1819年成立大哥倫比亞，委內瑞拉與新格拉納達的戰事牽制了西班牙的兵員，英國出於打開南美市場的算盤，向兩方都售賣火器並由英國船隻承擔運輸，智利海軍在科克倫率領下封鎖瓜亞基爾與卡亞俄，掐斷西班牙的海上補給。第三層是直接的導火線：1820年3月西班牙本土的憲章革命與斐迪南七世復位，使殖民地官員與軍官在效忠對象上出現分歧，基多與瓜亞基爾先後舉事；1821年底起秘魯方向派出的皇家派援軍越過安第斯南下，逼近基多，蘇克雷不得不迎戰，1822年5月24日在皮欎查遭遇。
causeEn: To understand why this war was fought, three layers of cause have to be stacked on top of each other. The deepest is the fissure inside the empire itself: the liberal revolution set off by the abdication of Ferdinand VII in 1808, the drain the Napoleonic wars put on Spain's overseas capacity, the quarrel between criollos and peninsulares over taxation, office and the monopoly of trade, and the long grip of the Audiencia of Quito on the city, all of which made it possible to ask the question of whether one should go on obeying Madrid. After the audiencias of Spanish America were abolished in 1814, an autonomous government in Quito was established and then collapsed; the Bolivian revolution of 1809 and Bolivian independence in 1825 supplied a precedent; and in 1811 Rocafuerte abolished slavery and the slave trade in Quito, which gave enslaved and mixed-race people a plain reason to side with the patriots. By 1820 these grievances in Quito had ripened into a political force that could be lit. The second layer is international: Bolívar founded Gran Colombia in 1819, the wars in Venezuela and New Granada tied down Spanish troops, Britain, in the hope of opening the South American market, sold arms to both sides and had its own ships carry the cargo, and the Chilean squadron under Cochrane blockaded Guayaquil and Callao, cutting the Spanish sea supply. The third layer is the immediate spark: the constitutional revolution in Spain in March 1820 and the restoration of Ferdinand VII divided colonial officials and officers over whom to obey, and Quito and Guayaquil rose in turn; from the end of 1821 the royalist reinforcements sent south out of Peru crossed the Andes and closed on Quito, Sucre had no choice but to meet them, and on 24 May 1822 they met at Pichincha.
impact: 皮欎查的勝利把南美解放運動的重心從北岸移到了安第斯。蘇克雷隨即率軍沿海岸推進，把基多、瓜亞基爾與內陸之間的通路打通，玻利瓦爾得以在1826年胡寧以及1827年胡寧與波托西諸役中以厄瓜多爾為基地攻入秘魯，秘魯的獨立因而不由秘魯本土的隊伍完成，而是由安第斯另一側的軍隊完成，這一點深刻影響了後來安第斯各國之間的邊界糾紛。制度上，厄瓜多爾把1811年廢奴的傳統帶進新國家，之後的「自由胎兒」安排在法律上承認奴隸所生子女為自由人，影響遠及加勒比與巴西的廢奴運動；厄瓜多爾是西屬美洲最早廢除奴隸制度的殖民地之一，這一傳統成了新國家的正當性來源之一。政治上，1822年的大哥倫比亞聯邦把委內瑞拉、新格拉納達、基多與瓜亞基爾綁在一起，卻也種下分裂的種子：1830年瓜亞基爾議定書之後，蘇克雷退出聯邦權力核心，玻利瓦爾病逝，厄瓜多爾與委內瑞拉之間的邊界爭端隨即浮上檯面，1834至1835年弗洛雷斯與總統波索爾福之間爆發內戰，1836年秘魯的玻利維爾領導聯邦干涉又使裂痕加深。長期看，這場戰爭為「自由軍」的政治傳統埋下伏筆：獨立後的厄瓜多爾軍隊被解散，軍人大量流入委內瑞拉與拉丁美洲各地，此後數十年裡的每一次拉美內戰都有這批老兵的身影。裝備層面的遺產同樣長久，厄瓜多爾與大哥倫比亞的軍隊在獨立後仍大量沿用英國燧發步槍與舊式火繩獵槍，線式操演的傳統一直延續到十九世紀中葉以後。
impactEn: The victory at Pichincha moved the centre of gravity of the South American wars of independence from the northern shore to the Andes. Sucre drove along the coast behind it and opened the line between Quito and Guayaquil, and Bolívar was able to use Ecuador as a base for the invasion of Peru in the Junín campaign of 1826 and the Junín and Potosí campaigns of 1827. Peru's independence was therefore not achieved by a Peruvian army but by an army from the far side of the Andes, a fact that shaped the border disputes among the Andean republics down to the present. Institutionally, Ecuador carried the abolition of 1811 into the new state, and the later free-womb rule, which in law recognised the children of enslaved mothers as free, reached the abolitionist movements in the Caribbean and in Brazil; Ecuador was among the first Spanish American colonies to abolish slavery, and that inheritance became one of the sources of the new country's legitimacy. Politically, the federation of Gran Colombia created in 1822 bound Venezuela, New Granada, Quito and Guayaquil together, and it planted the seed of the rupture as well: after the Guayaquil Protocol of 1830, Sucre withdrew from the centre of federal power, Bolívar died of illness, and the boundary dispute between Ecuador and Venezuela came to the surface, with civil war breaking out between Flores and President Posada in 1834 and 1835 and the Bolivarian federation of Peru intervening in 1836 to widen the breach. In the long run the war laid the groundwork for the politics of the free-lance soldier: the Ecuadorian army was disbanded after independence and its men dispersed across Venezuela and the rest of Latin America, and the old veterans of Pichincha turn up in every civil war of the following decades. The legacy in arms is just as durable, with the armies of Ecuador and Gran Colombia after independence still carrying large quantities of British flintlock muskets and old matchlock hunting guns, and the tradition of linear drill surviving well into the later decades of the nineteenth century.
result: 就1820至1822年這一輪而言，結果是愛國派完勝。1820年8月10日基多舉事成功，殖民當局退守一隅後撤出城市，基多成立自治執委會，克里奧爾精英第一次以武裝行動證明基多可以脫離馬德里；1821年9月24日瓜亞基爾起義成功，瓜亞基爾建立自治政府，國王派退出海岸線；1822年5月24日至25日皮欎查一戰，蘇克雷以約兩千人擊敗梅希亞的四千餘人，5月24日基多宣布厄瓜多爾共和國成立，隨後愛國派肅清安第斯山區的殘餘據點，1822年9月21日波哥大條約把新共和國併入大哥倫比亞聯邦，玻利瓦爾任聯邦總統、蘇克雷任元帥。西班牙在本土之外的殘餘勢力退往秘魯，此後只靠加勒比與秘魯的據點維持，其在南美大陸的崩解已不可逆轉。戰利品裡有大批英國燧發步槍與火炮，日後成為厄瓜多爾建軍的底子，也讓英國在南美的軍火市場大開；科克倫率領的智利海軍以及後來的英國自願兵為南美各國提供了海權與海上封鎖的樣板，這在歐洲人看來是把殖民警兵帶到了新大陸。代價也很明顯：厄瓜多爾幾乎沒有海軍、沒有兵工廠、沒有可用的現金，卻背上了巨額戰債與領土爭端；古城與產業在戰亂中損耗，軍隊在勝利後即告解散；1829年與1831年的秘魯戰爭中，厄瓜多爾在塔爾基一役再度落敗，1832年《安孔條約》才把加拉帕戈斯群島與部分邊界問題一併了結，國家獨立的帳單，用了整整十二年才結清。
resultEn: For the campaign of 1820 to 1822 the result was a complete patriot victory. The rising of 10 August 1820 in Quito succeeded, the colonial authorities withdrew and left the city, and Quito set up an autonomous junta, so that for the first time the criollo elite proved by arms that Quito could stand apart from Madrid. The rising at Guayaquil on 24 September 1821 succeeded, Guayaquil established its autonomous government, and the royalists were driven off the coastal plain. At Pichincha on 24 and 25 May 1822 Sucre defeated Aymerich's four thousand men with roughly two thousand of his own; on 24 May Quito proclaimed the Republic of Ecuador, and the patriots afterwards rooted out the remaining royalist strongholds in the Andes. The Treaty of Bogotá of 21 September 1822 drew the new republic into the federation of Gran Colombia, with Bolívar as president and Sucre as marshal. The last Spanish strength outside the Peninsula withdrew into Peru and thereafter survived only on its Caribbean and Peruvian footholds, and its collapse in the South American mainland could no longer be reversed. The booty included large quantities of British flintlock muskets and cannon, which later formed the stock of the Ecuadorian army, and it opened the South American arms market to British makers; the Chilean squadron under Cochrane, and the British volunteers who followed him, gave the South American republics a model of sea power and naval blockade, which struck Europeans as the carrying of colonial soldiery to a new continent. The costs were plain as well. Ecuador possessed almost no navy, no arsenal and no usable cash, yet it carried an enormous war debt and unresolved territorial claims; the old cities and the economy suffered in the fighting, and the army was dissolved as soon as the war was won. In the Peruvian war of 1829 and 1831 Ecuador was beaten again at Tarqui, and only the Treaty of Ancón of 1832 settled the Galapagos islands and part of the boundary questions together. The bill for independence was twelve years long before it was finally paid.
